title: Great American Family Selects CTS For Channel Origination, Playout, Transmission
body_html:
Why This Matters Right Now

The decision by Great American Family to outsource its channel origination, playout, and transmission to a third-party provider like CTS reflects a growing trend in the broadcast industry. As media companies face increasing pressure to deliver high-quality content across multiple platforms, they are seeking ways to streamline their operations and reduce costs. By outsourcing non-core functions, broadcasters can focus on their core competencies, such as content creation and programming, while leveraging the expertise and economies of scale of specialized providers. This approach can help reduce the complexity and risk associated with managing complex technical operations, allowing broadcasters to concentrate on what they do best: creating engaging content for their audiences. The move towards outsourcing technical operations is also driven by the need for greater flexibility and scalability in broadcast workflows. With the rise of over-the-top (OTT) and online video platforms, broadcasters need to be able to deliver content to a wide range of devices and platforms, while also maintaining the quality and reliability of their linear broadcasts. By partnering with a provider like CTS, Great American Family can potentially reduce the number of manual handoffs and improve metadata flow, leading to more predictable output under deadline pressure. This can be particularly important in a newsroom or live production environment, where timely and accurate delivery of content is critical. The outsourcing of technical operations also raises important questions about the role of the broadcaster in the content delivery chain. As media companies increasingly rely on third-party providers to manage their technical operations, they must carefully evaluate the potential risks and benefits of such partnerships. This includes considering factors such as validation, rollback, observability, and staff readiness to ensure a smooth transition and minimize disruption to existing operations. By taking a measured and informed approach to technical partnerships, broadcasters can harness the benefits of outsourcing while maintaining control over their core operations and ensuring the highest levels of quality and reliability.

Under the Hood: How It Actually Works

The partnership between Great American Family and CTS involves the integration of CTS's systems with the broadcaster's existing media asset management (MAM) and production asset management (PAM) systems, as well as its OTT and linear broadcast platforms. This integration enables the seamless communication of metadata and content between different systems, allowing for more efficient and automated workflows. The use of standardized protocols such as SMPTE ST 2110 and AES67 may also be relevant in this context, enabling high-quality audio and video transmission and ensuring compatibility between different systems. The channel origination, playout, and transmission services provided by CTS are likely to involve a range of technical components, including ingest, processing, and delivery systems. These systems work together to receive, process, and transmit content to the desired platforms, whether linear, OTT, or online. The specific technical details of the CTS system are not publicly disclosed, but it is likely that they involve a combination of hardware and software components, including servers, storage systems, and network infrastructure. By leveraging CTS's expertise and infrastructure, Great American Family can potentially reduce its technical complexity and improve the reliability of its broadcast operations. The integration of CTS's systems with Great American Family's existing infrastructure is critical to the success of the partnership. This requires careful planning and execution to ensure that the different systems can communicate effectively and work together seamlessly. The use of standardized protocols and APIs can help to facilitate this integration, enabling the different systems to exchange metadata and content in a consistent and reliable manner. By getting this integration right, Great American Family can unlock the full benefits of the partnership, including improved efficiency, reduced costs, and enhanced reliability.

What This Looks Like in a Real Broadcast Operation

In a real broadcast operation, the partnership between Great American Family and CTS might play out in a number of different ways. For example, in a newsroom environment, the CTS system might be used to ingest and process live feeds from the field, before transmitting them to the broadcaster's linear and OTT platforms. The system might also be used to manage the broadcaster's archive of pre-recorded content, allowing producers to easily search and retrieve clips for use in live broadcasts. By automating many of the technical tasks associated with broadcast operations, the CTS system can help to reduce the workload of newsroom staff, allowing them to focus on creating high-quality content for their audiences. In a live production environment, the CTS system might be used to manage the complex workflows associated with broadcasting live events. This might include ingesting and processing multiple live feeds, before transmitting them to the broadcaster's linear and OTT platforms. The system might also be used to manage the broadcaster's graphics and branding, allowing producers to easily add logos, tickers, and other visual elements to live broadcasts. By providing a flexible and scalable platform for live production, the CTS system can help to reduce the technical risks associated with broadcasting live events, while also improving the quality and consistency of the output. The use of the CTS system can also have important implications for the broadcaster's OTT and online operations. By providing a single, integrated platform for managing both linear and OTT workflows, the CTS system can help to reduce the complexity and cost of delivering content to multiple platforms. The system might also be used to manage the broadcaster's content delivery network (CDN), allowing producers to easily distribute content to a wide range of devices and platforms. By providing a flexible and scalable platform for OTT and online delivery, the CTS system can help to improve the reach and engagement of the broadcaster's content, while also reducing the technical risks associated with online delivery.

The Practical Impact: Cost, Speed, and Scale

The partnership between Great American Family and CTS has the potential to deliver a number of important benefits, including reduced costs, improved speed, and increased scale. By outsourcing its technical operations to a specialized provider, the broadcaster can potentially reduce its capital and operational expenditures, while also improving the efficiency and reliability of its broadcast operations. The use of standardized protocols and APIs can also help to reduce the complexity and cost of integrating different systems, allowing the broadcaster to more easily adapt to changing technical requirements. The CTS system can also help to improve the speed and agility of the broadcaster's operations, allowing producers to more quickly respond to changing market conditions and audience demands.
